subject: Next steps: coaching plan and checkpoints for Dylan Brooks

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Cc: sharon.lee@peopleadvisors.co
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Coaching support for Dylan Brooks — proposed pre-PIP steps

Hi Marissa / Vivek,

I wanted to loop you in early about Dylan Brooks (Eng, Platform) — we've documented several missed deadlines and quality regressions over the past two quarters. Before any formal PIP conversation, I want to run a short, structured coaching path so we can be confident we've given clear expectations and decent runway.

Proposed approach (2–4 week minimum):
- Week 0: align on specific outcomes (deliverables, quality bar, communication expectations).
- Weekly 1: focused 1:1 with measurable tasks and examples; manager provides concrete suggestions and resource assignments.
- Weekly 2: mid-point review with artifact-based feedback and one small, time-boxed assignment.
- End: final review to decide next steps (sustain, extend coaching, or move to formal PIP).

I'd like HR to review the proposed template so we capture documentation and ensure fairness; Sharon from PeopleAdvisors is CC'd if we want an external facilitator or legal posture later. Attaching a lightweight coaching template I used previously.

Can we schedule a short alignment call tomorrow or Friday? I prefer to start the first 1:1 with Dylan next week.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Performance coaching kickoff — clarity and short-term expectations

Dylan,

I want to schedule a focused coaching kickoff to set clear expectations and support you for the next few weeks. This is not a disciplinary notice — it's a time-limited coaching plan to help you get back on track.

Key points for our kickoff (30 minutes):
- Specific examples where work missed the expected quality or timelines (I will bring PRs and ticket numbers).
- Two clear outcomes we want to see over the next 3 weeks: 1) consistent on-time delivery of assigned sprint stories; 2) reduction in post-merge defects to under 2 per week for your modules.
- Weekly 1: manager-led pairing / code review sessions (2x 1 hour) and a small, time-boxed bugfix assignment.
- Weekly 2: mid-point review and written notes from both sides.

Please reply with your availability tomorrow or Wednesday and bring any context you think is helpful. HR (Marissa) will attend to ensure the process is fair and documented.

We value your contributions, Dylan — the goal here is to be explicit about expectations and give you the support to meet them.

Thanks,
Lauren
VP, Platform Engineering

Subject: Coaching progress update & next steps (wrap-up of 3-week run)

Team / Dylan,

Following our three-week coaching run (kickoff 14 Jan, mid-point 21 Jan, wrap 2 Feb), I wanted to summarize outcomes and propose next steps. Attached are the meeting notes and the filled coaching-template.

High level:
- Wins: Dylan adopted the short pairing sessions and completed the time-boxed bugfix assignment; several PRs merged with lower rework.
- Remaining gaps: delivery cadence is improved but still misses a sprint story on one critical ticket; defect count dropped but averaged ~2.5/week on the tracked modules (target was <2).
- Employee feedback: Dylan said blockers around unclear upstream ownership and shifted priorities contributed to delays; we assigned follow-ups to the product manager to reduce context-switching.

Recommendation: given partial progress but measurable gaps, I propose one of two paths: 1) extend the coaching period by 2 weeks with a tightened checklist and daily morning stand-ins for the owner of the critical ticket; or 2) move to a formal PIP if the next two-week extension does not yield the target metrics.

Please respond with preference; HR recommends extension with clearly defined metrics and daily check-ins before escalating. I appreciate everyone's partnership here.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Platform Engineering
